headword: I'll take your word for it
definition: said when you believe someone without checking the facts yourself
example:
A: This restaurant has the best pasta in town.
B: {{I'll}} {{take}} {{your}} {{word}} {{for}} {{it}}.
example2:
A: The movie is great, trust me.
B: I'll take your word for it.

definition: said to show you completely agree with what someone just said
example:
A: This city really needs more bike lanes.
B: {{I}} {{couldn't}} {{agree}} {{more}}.
example2:
A: Our manager explains things so clearly.
B: I couldn't agree more.

definition: said to show you understand and accept a reason
example:
A: We moved the meeting because the client is busy.
B: {{That}} {{makes}} {{sense}}.
example2:
A: I'll leave early to avoid traffic.
B: That makes sense.

definition: said when a piece of advice sounds simple but is hard to follow
example:
A: Just stop worrying about the exam.
B: {{That's}} {{easier}} {{said}} {{than}} {{done}}.
example2:
A: Why don't you quit and start your own business?
B: That's easier said than done.

meanings.ja: 言うは易く行うは難し

definition: said when you leave a person you will meet again soon
example:
A: I have to go to class now.
B: OK. {{See}} {{you}} {{later}}!
example2:
A: Bye, Tom.
B: See you later!

definition: a polite way to say no or give bad news
example:
A: Is there a later train tonight?
B: {{I'm}} {{afraid}} {{not}}.
example2:
A: Can I change my seat?
B: I'm afraid not; the flight is full.

meanings.ja: 残念ながら、そうではありません

definition: said to show you will remember some advice for later
example:
A: The office closes early on Fridays.
B: Thanks, {{I'll}} {{keep}} {{that}} {{in}} {{mind}}.
example2:
A: Book early, because tickets sell out fast.
B: Good tip, I'll keep that in mind.

definition: a friendly way to ask someone how they are
example:
A: Hey, Tom! {{How's}} {{it}} {{going}}?
B: Not bad, thanks.
example2:
A: How's it going with the new job?
B: Pretty well, actually.

definition: said to accept an opinion or request you do not fully share
example:
A: I'd rather not work this Saturday.
B: {{Fair}} {{enough}}. I'll ask someone else.
example2:
A: I don't like spicy food.
B: Fair enough. We'll order something mild.

meanings.ja: まあいいよ・なるほどね

definition: said when you let someone else make the decision
example:
A: Should we get pizza or sushi?
B: {{It's}} {{up}} {{to}} {{you}}.
example2: You can stay or go home; it's up to you.

definition: said when you doubt that something hoped for will really happen
example:
A: He promised to pay me back soon.
B: {{I}} {{won't}} {{hold}} {{my}} {{breath}}.
example2:
A: They say the road will be fixed this month.
B: I won't hold my breath.

definition: said to get someone's attention in a polite way
example:
A: {{Excuse}} {{me}}, where is the bus stop?
B: It is over there.
example2:
A: Excuse me, is this seat free?
B: Yes, please sit down.

definition: said when you strongly agree because you have the same bad experience
example:
A: This traffic is awful today.
B: {{Tell}} {{me}} {{about}} {{it}}. I've waited an hour.
example2:
A: Mondays are so hard.
B: Tell me about it.

meanings.ja: まったくだよ・わかる

definition: said when you are not sure that what you just said is correct
example:
A: When does the store open?
B: Around nine, but {{don't}} {{quote}} {{me}} {{on}} {{that}}.
example2:
A: How far is the station?
B: Maybe two miles. Don't quote me on that.

definition: said to tell someone that you feel that way too
example:
A: I'm so tired today.
B: {{Same}} {{here}}.
example2:
A: I can't wait for the holidays.
B: Same here!

definition: said to agree with a plan that someone has just told you
example:
A: Let's meet at six for dinner.
B: {{Sounds}} {{good}}!
example2:
A: We can go to the beach on Sunday.
B: Sounds good to me.

definition: said when you meet someone again after many months or years
example:
A: {{Long}} {{time}} {{no}} {{see}}! How have you been?
B: Great, thanks.
example2:
A: Long time no see!
B: I know, it's been years.

definition: said to show you are glad for something someone gave or did
example:
A: Here is your tea.
B: {{Thank}} {{you}}.
example2:
A: This is a present for you.
B: Thank you very much!

definition: said before something that might be misunderstood or sound rude
example:
A: So you don't like the plan?
B: {{Don't}} {{get}} {{me}} {{wrong}}, it's good, but it's expensive.
example2: Don't get me wrong, I like my job, but the hours are long.

definition: a casual way to ask what is new or what is wrong
example:
A: {{What's}} {{up}}?
B: Not much. I'm just watching TV.
example2:
A: Hey, what's up? You look tired.
B: I stayed up late.

definition: said to tell someone that a thing is not important now
example:
A: What did you say?
B: {{Never}} {{mind}}. It wasn't important.
example2:
A: I can't find my pen.
B: Never mind, I have another one.

definition: said in a shop when you decide to buy something
example:
A: This jacket is twenty percent off today.
B: Great, {{I'll}} {{take}} {{it}}.
example2:
A: The room has a view of the sea.
B: Perfect, I'll take it.

definition: said to tell someone that something is not a problem
example:
A: Sorry, I forgot to call you back.
B: {{No}} {{worries}}.
example2:
A: Thanks for waiting.
B: No worries, I just got here.

headword: couldn't have said it better myself
definition: said to praise what someone said as exactly what you think
example:
A: Honest feedback helps people grow, even if it stings.
B: {{Couldn't}} {{have}} {{said}} {{it}} {{better}} {{myself}}.
example2:
A: Good teams trust each other first.
B: Couldn't have said it better myself.

meanings.ja: 私もそう言いたかった

definition: said to accept that someone's argument is reasonable
example:
A: We can't afford a bigger office yet.
B: {{That's}} {{a}} {{fair}} {{point}}.
example2:
A: Remote workers need clear rules too.
B: That's a fair point; I'll draft some.
